pr_title: A quick fix to add more known connector libraries to ADO.NET
pr_body:
This is a quick fix to add some known alternative connector libraries
to SQL Server and MySQL ADO.NET providers. The values are still hard-coded
and the real fix would to provide similar defaults but have a developer
configuration surface.

Fixes #6229 and #6230.
pr_comments:
This is a 15 minutes coding fix (of which five minutes went for waiting IntelliSense, something in the sln that causes slowness?) and I have not run the tests. Should give at least an idea how to get everyone out of the immediate trouble. Have to run now, but will be around later today and during the week to give some testing.

Ping @ReubenBond, @sergeybykov.

Looking at https://github.com/dotnet/orleans/pull/6238 is an alternative. Have to reflect this a bit since have to check thow this _invariant name_ or _well-known stable_ should be seen outside. I.e. that there isn't accidentally a new invariant on the configuration surface if it should be removed in a short while. Some discussion at https://github.com/npgsql/npgsql/issues/2358, for instance.

This also needs to actually update the information on asynchronous operation as per connector library.

Throwing this here quickly: https://github.com/dotnet/SqlClient/issues/239. So it looks like a new invariant should be introduced as @voronov-maxim has changed. This wouldn't also work due to namespace change. So let's close this in favour of Maxim's, but let's see if we could add MySql too. :)
